protocol.py: 2 biology problems (2 notes).

1. NOTE CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 95 stocks
   line 59:  p20.aspirate(5, src_well)
   At line 59 the tip went into source_A2 (well A2 in slot 3), source_A3 (well A3 in slot
   3), source_A4 (well A4 in slot 3), source_A5 (well A5 in slot 3) and 91 more while it
   still carried lb (well A1 in slot 1), source_A1 (well A1 in slot 3), source_A2 (well A2
   in slot 3), source_A3 (well A3 in slot 3) and 92 more from an earlier step (this line did
   it 95 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid
   it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn
   from them then took the unwanted material along into 95 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4,
   A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 87 more in slot 2.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 87 more in slot 3.
   Also reached 95 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 87 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 59 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [7bb53da31b6d]

2. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 94 wells never mixed after source_A1, source_A2, source_A3,
source_A4 and 90 more went in (1% of the well)
   line 60:  p20.dispense(5, dest_well)
   At line 60 the robot added source_A1, source_A2, source_A3, source_A4 and 90 more to
   wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 2, which already held lb (this
   line did it 94 times). The addition was 1% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   If the plate is vortexed and spun down before it is used, nothing is wrong; if it goes
   straight to the instrument, the wells are not what the protocol says they are.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 2 after line 60:
   `mix_after=(5, 404)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 404, well)`, with the volume
   about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [be2f9bcb250c]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
